transactions.title: A different Philadelphia franchise.
transactions.text: The San Francisco Warriors send Chamberlain to the 76ers for Dierking, Neumann, Shaffer’s player rights and cash. Philadelphia here is a different franchise from the Warriors.

moves.note: Player rights after his NBA departure; not draft rights.

notes: The effective date follows Golden State’s historical transaction ledger. Philadelphia here means the 76ers; the Warriors had previously played in Philadelphia.

transactions.title: The biggest name moves again.
transactions.text: Philadelphia sends Chamberlain to Los Angeles. Imhoff, Clark, Chambers and cash make up the Lakers’ return package.

transactions.title: A skyhook changes coast.
transactions.text: Milwaukee sends Abdul-Jabbar and Wesley to Los Angeles. Two veterans, two sets of rookie rights and cash form the return.

transactions.title: Follow the rookie in the return.
transactions.text: Nine years later, Bridgeman joins Johnson and Catchings in a Clippers package. Cummings, Hodges and Pierce head to Milwaukee.
notes: The Clippers had relocated to Los Angeles by this transaction. Later Cummings trades are outside this bounded route.

transactions.title: Five and eight change hands.
transactions.text: Seattle sends Pippen’s draft rights to Chicago. Polynice’s rights, a second-round obligation and a protected first-round swap go the other way.
notes: Pippen was selected fifth and Polynice eighth. This records the completed draft-night rights exchange, not the pre-draft agreement.
The future second and swap are retained separately. Their later transfers and selections are outside the published route.

transactions.title: Barkley heads west.
transactions.text: Philadelphia sends Barkley to Phoenix for Hornacek, Perry and Lang. Four years later, another package will take him to Houston.

transactions.title: Detroit and San Antonio exchange forwards.
transactions.text: Rodman goes to the Spurs. Elliott and Wood go to Detroit, while San Antonio also receives draft consideration with a protected swap.
notes: The companion Isaiah Morris exchange is recorded separately, following the contemporaneous Associated Press account. Later team summaries combine the two same-day exchanges.
The 1994 second’s original conditional trigger is unconfirmed here. The protected swap’s possible 1994–96 years are not represented as three different first-round assets.

transactions.title: A separate exchange on the same day.
transactions.text: Detroit sends Morris to San Antonio for a conditional second. It accompanies the Rodman news, but has its own consideration.

transactions.title: Elliott returns before Rodman leaves.
transactions.shortTitle: Sean Elliott goes back to San Antonio
transactions.text: Detroit sends Elliott back to San Antonio. The Spurs send Curley’s draft rights and a 1997 second-round consideration.
notes: The completed July 19 report and later Spurs transaction ledger are used. An earlier guide’s player biography lists July 18. The canceled February 1994 Houston proposal is not a completed trade and creates no edge.

transactions.title: The Worm changes sides.
transactions.text: Chicago acquires Rodman from San Antonio. Perdue and an undisclosed additional consideration go to the Spurs.
notes: The Spurs ledger and contemporary completed report give October 2. The additional consideration is preserved as undisclosed. Jack Haley’s separate free-agent signing is not placed in this exchange.

transactions.title: The name is called in Charlotte.
transactions.text: Charlotte selects Kobe Bryant at No. 13. The draft selection and the eventual rights transfer have different effective dates.

transactions.title: Thirteen becomes a Laker.
transactions.shortTitle: Kobe’s rights go to Los Angeles
transactions.text: Los Angeles sends Vlade Divac to Charlotte for Bryant’s draft rights. A straight exchange with a long basketball afterlife.
notes: Charlotte’s official historical record lists July 11 as the rights trade date. This story ends at the transfer; later free agency is not drawn as a trade return.

transactions.title: Houston sends a whole rotation.
transactions.text: Barkley and a second-round obligation go to Houston. Cassell, Horry, Bryant and Brown move to Phoenix; Cassell soon enters the Kidd exchange.

transactions.title: Dallas breaks up the backcourt.
transactions.text: Kidd heads to Phoenix in a six-player exchange. Dallas receives Finley, Green, Cassell and a conditional second. Cassell’s stay will be brief.

transactions.title: Nine players change addresses.
transactions.text: Less than two months later, Cassell joins four other Mavericks on the way to New Jersey. Bradley, Pack, Reeves and O’Bannon come to Dallas.

transactions.title: A Dallas draft choice enters the trail.
transactions.shortTitle: Dallas sends Cato’s rights to Portland
transactions.text: Dallas trades Cato’s draft rights to Portland for Anstey’s rights and cash. Cato will later travel in two star-sized packages.

transactions.title: No. 53: Greg Buckner
transactions.text: The Phoenix-origin second settles at No. 53. Dallas selects Greg Buckner.

transactions.title: Dallas bets on the unknown.
transactions.text: The Mavericks exchange No. 6 for two sets of draft rights. One belongs to Dirk. The other is already headed into another deal.

transactions.title: The other half of draft night.
transactions.text: Garrity’s rights join two players and a future first. Phoenix sends Steve Nash to Dallas in a separate exchange.

transactions.title: Chicago’s chapter closes.
transactions.text: The Bulls sign and trade Pippen to Houston. Rogers and a future second-round consideration come to Chicago.
notes: Pippen was signed and traded. The transaction date follows the completed January 22 report and Houston’s ledger.
Sources disagree about the second-round consideration’s year. Its existence is documented; its origin, conditional mechanism and eventual selection remain untraced.

transactions.title: No. 9: Shawn Marion
transactions.text: The first Dallas sent for Nash becomes Phoenix’s No. 9 selection: Shawn Marion.

transactions.title: Six players go the other way.
transactions.text: Houston trades Pippen to Portland. Its return includes Cato, the former Dallas draft choice, alongside five teammates.

transactions.title: Two point guards, five players.
transactions.text: Phoenix sends Kidd and Dudley to New Jersey. Marbury, Newman and Samake go the other way.

transactions.title: Seven players. One new pairing.
transactions.text: McGrady, Howard, Lue and Gaines move from Orlando to Houston. Francis, Mobley and Cato form the package going to Orlando.

transactions.title: The dynasty splits.
transactions.text: Shaq leaves Los Angeles. One player in Miami’s return package, Caron Butler, will later join another exchange.
notes: The Lakers’ historical guide also records Miami’s 2007 second-round pick; it is included alongside the better-known 2006 first.

transactions.title: Vince leaves Toronto.
transactions.shortTitle: Vince Carter goes to New Jersey
transactions.text: New Jersey adds Carter. Toronto receives Mourning, two Williamses and protected firsts originating with Philadelphia and Denver.

transactions.title: No. 16: Joey Graham
transactions.text: The Philadelphia-origin first conveys at No. 16. Toronto selects Joey Graham.

transactions.title: A bridge named Caron Butler.
transactions.text: Butler and Atkins go to Washington. Brown and Profit move to Los Angeles. The bridge runs through a package, not Butler alone.
notes: The Wizards page carries a July 29 publication date; the completed sign-and-trade took effect August 2.

transactions.title: Orlando’s return takes another turn.
transactions.text: Francis goes to New York. Orlando receives Ariza and Hardaway; Ariza’s next trade will take him to Los Angeles.

transactions.title: No. 26: Jordan Farmar
transactions.text: Miami’s first becomes No. 26. The Lakers select Jordan Farmar.

transactions.title: The second takes a Dallas detour.
transactions.text: Dallas sends Pinnock’s draft rights to Los Angeles. The Miami second from the Shaq package goes the other way.

transactions.title: The Answer leaves Philadelphia.
transactions.text: Iverson and McFarlin go to Denver. Philadelphia receives Miller, Smith and two firsts with different franchise origins.

transactions.title: No. 21: Daequan Cook
transactions.text: Denver’s first becomes Philadelphia’s No. 21 selection. Cook’s draft rights are about to enter another exchange.

transactions.title: No. 50: Renaldas Seibutis
transactions.text: Dallas uses the Miami-origin second at No. 50 on Renaldas Seibutis. This branch ends with his draft rights.

transactions.title: One spot in the draft. Three assets.
transactions.text: Miami trades Smith’s draft rights for Cook’s rights, a future second and cash. The Denver pick’s player heads to South Florida.
notes: Smith was selected No. 20; Cook was No. 21. The future second is 2009, as Miami’s transaction ledger states.

transactions.title: Boston goes all in.
transactions.text: Five players, a Boston first, a returned Minnesota obligation and cash go west. Garnett joins Boston, then becomes part of the 2013 Brooklyn package.

resolutions.detail: Returned to Minnesota: Boston relinquishes the prior claim on Minnesota’s own conditional first.

transactions.title: Ariza enters the Lakers chapter.
transactions.text: Orlando trades Ariza to Los Angeles for Cook and Evans. The connection runs through Francis’s earlier package.

transactions.title: One Gasol for another.
transactions.text: Pau heads to Los Angeles. Memphis receives a package containing his younger brother’s draft rights, three players and two firsts.
notes: Marc is represented as draft rights at this moment. Cash and the Memphis second-round pick are part of the exchange, even though they rarely make the headline.

transactions.title: Two old branches cross.
transactions.text: Shaq goes to Phoenix. Marion, selected with the Dallas first from the Nash exchange, moves to Miami with Banks.

transactions.title: The long way back to Dallas.
transactions.text: Kidd returns with Allen and Wright. Five Dallas players, two first-round obligations and cash form the return package.
notes: Keith Van Horn was signed and traded. This is the completed February 19 package, after the earlier proposal involving Devean George was abandoned.

transactions.title: No. 21: Ryan Anderson
transactions.text: Dallas’s first conveys at No. 21. New Jersey selects Ryan Anderson, who will join a much larger headline a year later.

transactions.title: Iverson and Billups cross paths.
transactions.text: Denver sends Iverson to Detroit. Billups, McDyess and Samb head to Denver. Billups later joins the Carmelo Anthony package.

transactions.title: The same two players move again.
transactions.shortTitle: Marion and Banks go to Toronto
transactions.text: Marion and Banks go to Toronto. Miami receives Jermaine O’Neal, Moon and conditional draft consideration.
notes: Miami generated a reported $4.2 million traded-player exception. An exception is cap capacity created by a transaction; it is not a player or pick transferred from another team.
Toronto’s first-round obligation is not followed further. Reports disagree on final-year protection wording; the known 2010 lottery protection and separate conditional second are retained.

transactions.title: A Dallas pick travels with Vince.
transactions.shortTitle: Carter and Anderson go to Orlando
transactions.text: Carter and Ryan Anderson go to Orlando together. Lee, Alston and Battie move to New Jersey. Anderson entered this route through Dallas’s Kidd trade.

transactions.title: Another stop for the Big Fella.
transactions.text: Cleveland acquires Shaq. Wallace, Pavlović, a second and cash go to Phoenix.

transactions.title: The Dallas pick comes home.
transactions.text: Marion reaches Dallas through a four-team sign-and-trade. The 1999 pick’s path has passed through Phoenix, Miami and Toronto.
notes: Marion and Türkoğlu were signed and traded. Cash directions follow the team media guides; amounts are not asserted.
Orlando also created a traded-player exception. This is generated cap capacity, not a transferable pick.

transactions.title: Butler’s branch reaches Dallas, too.
transactions.text: Washington sends three players and cash to Dallas. Four players leave the Mavericks in the exchange.

transactions.title: Nine players spread across three cities.
transactions.text: McGrady reaches New York. Houston receives Martin, Armstrong, Hill, Jeffries and draft consideration. Sacramento receives Landry, Dorsey, Hughes and cash.
notes: The final completed three-team package is one event. McGrady is not routed through Sacramento on the basis of an earlier proposal.
Martin and Hill later enter different packages. Neither alone represents the entire return from this exchange.

transactions.title: Cook travels with another first.
transactions.shortTitle: Cook and No. 18 go to Oklahoma City
transactions.text: Miami sends Cook and its No. 18 pick to Oklahoma City. The Minnesota-origin No. 32 pick goes to Miami.
notes: These are established draft positions on the eve of the draft. Later pick transfers are not collapsed into this exchange. Cook’s Oklahoma City departure is the existing 2012 Harden trade.

transactions.title: No. 28: Greivis Vásquez
transactions.text: The later Lakers first in the Gasol exchange becomes No. 28. Memphis selects Greivis Vásquez.

transactions.title: Six players. Another new jersey.
transactions.text: Carter, Gortat and Piétrus go to Phoenix with a first and cash. Richardson, Türkoğlu and Clark head to Orlando.
notes: Orlando’s separate Rashard Lewis–Gilbert Arenas trade on the same day is not merged into this package. Carter’s later Dallas arrival was free agency, not a return from this exchange.

transactions.title: Thirteen players. One headline.
transactions.shortTitle: Carmelo Anthony goes to New York
transactions.text: New York gets Anthony and five other players. Denver receives five players, three pick obligations and a swap right; Minnesota completes the final structure.
notes: This is the completed February 22 three-team exchange. The 2016 swap is a right to exchange two firsts, not an additional outright first for Denver.

transactions.title: Dallas sends a first into the future.
transactions.text: Dallas acquires Odom, a Lakers second and a later second-round swap. Its protected first begins a journey through three teams.
notes: Los Angeles generated a traded-player exception. That is cap capacity created by the deal, not a transferred asset.
The 2013 consideration is a second-round swap. The protected Dallas first is the same obligation later received by Houston and Oklahoma City.

transactions.title: Lob City gets its point guard.
transactions.shortTitle: Chris Paul arrives in Los Angeles
transactions.text: Paul heads to the Clippers. New Orleans receives Gordon, Aminu, Kaman and a first-round entitlement with two possible origins.
notes: The completed Clippers transaction is dated December 14. The earlier proposed Lakers transaction was not completed and creates no ownership edge.
New Orleans was called the Hornets. The two outgoing 2015 seconds are included; their later paths are outside this story.

transactions.title: A Christmas Eve exchange.
transactions.text: Vásquez goes to New Orleans for Pondexter. Two young players trade places.

transactions.title: The Dallas obligation moves again.
transactions.shortTitle: Hill for Fisher and Dallas’s first
transactions.text: Houston sends Hill to the Lakers. Fisher and the protected Dallas first go to Houston, where the pick will join the Harden package.

transactions.title: No. 17 stays with Dallas.
transactions.text: Dallas lands inside the top-20 protection. Houston still holds the future obligation; a new pick has not been added.

resolutions.detail: Dallas’s 2012 first is No. 17, within the protected range. The same obligation rolls to 2013.

transactions.title: No. 38: Quincy Miller
transactions.text: Denver uses the Golden State-origin second from the Anthony package on Quincy Miller at No. 38.

transactions.title: No. 10: Austin Rivers
transactions.text: The Minnesota-origin selection wins the comparison. New Orleans uses No. 10 on Austin Rivers.

transactions.title: No. 16: Royce White
transactions.text: New York’s first conveys outside the protected top five. Houston uses No. 16 on Royce White.

transactions.title: No. 55: Darius Johnson-Odom
transactions.text: The Lakers second from the Odom package conveys at No. 55. Dallas selects Darius Johnson-Odom.

transactions.title: The second’s player goes back to L.A.
transactions.shortTitle: Johnson-Odom’s rights return to Los Angeles
transactions.text: Dallas sends Johnson-Odom’s newly selected rights to the Lakers for cash. The draft selection and rights trade are separate events.
notes: Los Angeles’s historical transaction ledger dates the rights acquisition June 28. This follows the draft-night event date.

transactions.title: A sixth man gets his own team.
transactions.text: Houston acquires Harden with three other players. Oklahoma City takes Martin, Lamb and three pick obligations with very different conditions.

transactions.title: No. 12: Steven Adams
transactions.text: Toronto lands inside the permitted lottery range. Oklahoma City uses No. 12 on Steven Adams.

transactions.title: No. 32: Álex Abrines
transactions.text: The second-round asset in the Harden package becomes the rights to Álex Abrines.

transactions.title: The protection holds.
transactions.text: Dallas’s No. 13 first stays protected. Oklahoma City must wait; this is the same obligation, not an extra pick.

resolutions.detail: Dallas’s 2013 pick is No. 13, inside the protected 1–20 range. The obligation rolls to 2014.

transactions.title: The other half of the swap finds a home.
transactions.text: Toronto sends Bargnani to New York for three players and three pick obligations. Its 2016 first will be whichever pick Denver leaves behind.
notes: Quentin Richardson was signed and traded. Toronto receives one composite 2016 entitlement, not both New York’s and Denver’s picks.

transactions.title: Three teams make room for Evans.
transactions.text: Vásquez moves to Sacramento, Evans to New Orleans, and Lopez to Portland. Draft rights, seconds and cash complete the package.
notes: Evans was signed and traded. The final July 10 transaction is used, not the July 4 agreement. The published team summaries compress the secondary rights into draft consideration; Mark Deeks’s record supplies the two second-round swap rights.

transactions.title: Brooklyn buys the present.
transactions.text: Veterans go to Brooklyn. Boston receives five players, three future firsts and a swap right whose value will take years to emerge.
notes: Keith Bogans was signed and traded. The 2014 first remained subject to Atlanta’s prior swap rights. The conditional Boston second is included separately.

transactions.title: A seven-player reset.
transactions.shortTitle: Vásquez joins the Rudy Gay package
transactions.text: Vásquez moves again, this time to Toronto with three teammates. Gay, Acy and Gray go to Sacramento.

transactions.title: No. 21: Mitch McGary
transactions.text: No. 21 sits just outside the protection. Dallas’s obligation finally conveys.

transactions.title: No. 17: James Young
transactions.text: The first of the three outright Brooklyn obligations settles at No. 17.

transactions.title: One guard. Two separate futures.
transactions.shortTitle: Vásquez for Powell rights and a first
transactions.text: Milwaukee receives Vásquez. Toronto takes Powell’s draft rights and a protected Clippers first.

transactions.title: Two tickets, two destinations.
transactions.shortTitle: Denver gets No. 7; Toronto gets No. 9
transactions.text: The lottery fixes New York’s pick at No. 7 and Denver’s at No. 9. Denver takes No. 7; Toronto’s separate entitlement receives No. 9.

resolutions.detail: Denver takes New York’s No. 7 instead of its own No. 9. The No. 9 goes to Toronto under the subsequent Bargnani agreement.

notes: May 17 records the now-known lottery allocation. It is not presented as a separately verified administrative exercise date. Both sides of the exchange are shown; no third first-round pick is created.

transactions.title: No. 3: Jaylen Brown
transactions.text: Brooklyn’s 2016 obligation becomes No. 3. Boston selects Jaylen Brown.

transactions.title: New York’s pick becomes Murray.
transactions.text: Denver selects Jamal Murray at No. 7. The route begins with a swap clause in the Anthony trade five years earlier.

transactions.title: Denver’s pick becomes Poeltl.
transactions.text: Toronto selects Jakob Poeltl at No. 9. Two years later, he joins DeRozan and a first in the Leonard package.

transactions.title: The lottery fixes Boston’s position.
transactions.text: May 16 establishes the pick positions: Boston is allocated Brooklyn’s No. 1 through the swap. This is the lottery determination date, not a sourced administrative exercise date.

resolutions.detail: Boston receives Brooklyn’s No. 1; Brooklyn receives Boston’s No. 27. Boston’s No. 57 second-round selection also conveys.

notes: May 16 is the date the lottery established the positions. The swap was exercised for the 2017 draft; this scene records the now-known allocation.

transactions.title: Boston trades down.
transactions.text: The No. 1 selection changes hands again. Boston takes No. 3 and another conditional first-round entitlement.

transactions.title: No. 23: OG Anunoby
transactions.text: The Clippers first conveys at No. 23. Toronto selects OG Anunoby.

transactions.title: Chicago starts over.
transactions.text: Butler and the No. 16 draft rights go to Minnesota. Chicago receives LaVine, Dunn and the rights to Markkanen at No. 7.

transactions.title: Utah finds Mitchell at thirteen.
transactions.text: Denver’s selection becomes Utah’s new guard. The Jazz send Lyles and the No. 24 rights to Lydon in the same draft-night package.

transactions.title: The pick becomes Tatum.
transactions.text: Boston selects Jayson Tatum at No. 3. Brooklyn’s swap was one step in this route; Philadelphia’s trade-down deal was another.

transactions.title: One piece arrives from Detroit.
transactions.text: Houston acquires Hilliard for cash before including him in the Paul package.

transactions.title: Another piece arrives from Dallas.
transactions.text: Liggins moves from Dallas to Houston, then joins the same outgoing package as Hilliard.

transactions.title: One star. Seven players. Another first.
transactions.text: The Clippers receive seven players, a protected first and cash. Beverley and the first-round obligation become two very different paths out of Lob City.
notes: Paul opted into his existing contract before the trade. This was not a sign-and-trade.
Hilliard and Liggins had to reach Houston before Houston could trade them; same-day ordering represents that ownership dependency.

transactions.title: The first leaves Los Angeles almost immediately.
transactions.shortTitle: The Houston first joins the Gallinari deal
transactions.text: The Houston obligation joins Crawford, Stone and cash in Atlanta. Denver sends Gallinari to Los Angeles and receives a Washington-origin second.
notes: Gallinari was signed and traded by Denver. This is one three-team transaction.

transactions.title: A new running mate in Oklahoma.
transactions.text: Indiana trades Paul George for two young players. Two years later, Oklahoma City will send George into another, much larger exchange.

transactions.title: The last Brooklyn first leaves Boston.
transactions.shortTitle: Brooklyn first joins the Kyrie package
transactions.text: Boston includes the 2018 Brooklyn obligation in its Irving package. Cleveland receives three players and two draft assets.
notes: The August 22 proposal was amended. Miami’s 2020 second was added before completion on August 30; the joint announcement was published after midnight UTC.
Irving’s later Boston departure was free agency. This route follows the Brooklyn pick, not an invented trade from Boston to Brooklyn.

transactions.title: Melo moves. Another pick stays behind.
transactions.text: New York sends Anthony to Oklahoma City for Kanter, McDermott and Chicago’s 2018 second.

transactions.title: Not this lottery.
transactions.text: The Lakers’ pick lands at No. 10. Boston’s entitlement requires No. 2–5, so the same obligation moves to its 2019 comparison.

resolutions.detail: Lakers No. 10 is outside the 2018 conveyance range. The obligation now compares the Sacramento and Philadelphia 2019 firsts under the original terms.

transactions.title: Two picks. Two futures.
transactions.text: Dallas moves up from No. 5 to No. 3. The extra first-round obligation gives Atlanta a second path into the future.
notes: The draft took place June 21 in the United States. The NBA release timestamp is June 22 UTC. These are draft rights, not signed NBA contracts.

transactions.title: No. 36: Mitchell Robinson
transactions.text: The Chicago-origin second becomes No. 36. New York selects Mitchell Robinson.

transactions.title: No. 8: Collin Sexton
transactions.text: The third outright first from the 2013 Brooklyn trade becomes Cleveland’s No. 8 selection.

transactions.title: No. 30: Omari Spellman
transactions.text: Atlanta selects Spellman with the Houston-origin pick acquired in the Gallinari deal. The top-three protection never comes into play.

transactions.title: Toronto takes the leap.
transactions.text: Leonard and Green go north. San Antonio receives DeRozan, Poeltl and a protected first. Poeltl’s branch will eventually bend back.

transactions.title: One more three-team package.
transactions.text: Anthony and a protected first go to Atlanta. Schröder and Luwawu-Cabarrot reach Oklahoma City; Muscala goes to Philadelphia, with Anderson going to Atlanta.
notes: Anthony was subsequently waived by Atlanta. His later Houston signing is not drawn as a trade return.

transactions.title: Philadelphia makes its move.
transactions.text: Butler and Patton move together again. Covington, Šarić, Bayless and a conditional second-round entitlement form Minnesota’s return.
notes: November 12 is the completed trade date; November 10 was the reported agreement.

transactions.title: The younger brother moves north.
transactions.text: Eleven years after his rights arrived in Memphis, Marc goes to Toronto. Three players and a second-round obligation move the other way.

transactions.title: No. 29: Keldon Johnson
transactions.text: Toronto’s first lands at No. 29, outside the protection. San Antonio selects Keldon Johnson.

transactions.title: No. 14: Romeo Langford
transactions.text: Sacramento’s No. 14 satisfies the conditional entitlement. Boston selects Romeo Langford.

transactions.title: No. 10: Cam Reddish
transactions.text: The protection does not apply at No. 10. Atlanta uses the Dallas selection on Cam Reddish.

transactions.title: Four teams make Miami possible.
transactions.text: Butler joins Miami through a sign-and-trade. Richardson goes to Philadelphia, while Portland and the Clippers make the complete exchange work.
notes: This is the completed four-team structure. Earlier proposals involving Dallas did not become this transaction. Miami’s first later joins the Paul George package; subsequent protection amendments are outside this route.

transactions.title: Los Angeles makes its move.
transactions.text: Davis goes to Los Angeles in a three-team package. Players, draft rights, future obligations, a swap and cash all move.
notes: The deal became official July 6; the NBA repost is timestamped July 7 UTC. The Hunter rights later entered a separate Atlanta trade, outside this branch.

transactions.title: A departure leaves something behind.
transactions.shortTitle: Durant and Russell are signed and traded
transactions.text: Durant and Russell both participate in sign-and-trades. Golden State also receives Napier and Graham; Brooklyn receives a protected draft obligation.
notes: July 7 is the completed transaction date, distinct from the June 30 agreement and July 8 reporting update.
Durant’s earlier Oklahoma City departure was free agency and is not represented as a trade.

transactions.title: Spellman crosses another state line.
transactions.text: Golden State acquires Spellman for Damian Jones and a future second. This branch will meet the Russell branch in the next trade.
notes: The 2026 Golden State second shares its canonical identity with its much later Knicks–Charlotte appearance. The intervening transfers are not traced here.

transactions.title: The price of right now.
transactions.text: George goes to the Clippers. Oklahoma City receives Gilgeous-Alexander, Gallinari, five firsts and two swap rights.
notes: Miami’s 2023 obligation was later amended; the original contract terms are preserved here. Only the 2022 Clippers first is followed to a selection.

transactions.title: The point guards trade places.
transactions.text: Houston sends Paul and four future draft rights to Oklahoma City for Westbrook. One of the outright firsts will reach the 2024 lottery.
notes: July 16 is completion, rather than the July 11 reported agreement.
The final 2025 swap protects Houston’s top 10, correcting preliminary reports that described top-20 protection.
The potential $1 million payment is a conditional 2026 fallback, not cash paid in this transaction.

transactions.title: Two branches meet. Two more leave.
transactions.text: Russell, Spellman and Evans go to Minnesota together. Golden State receives Wiggins and two Minnesota draft obligations.
notes: Wiggins and the picks are the return for the entire three-player package. No single outgoing player is credited with producing the whole return.

transactions.title: The point guard gets another new address.
transactions.text: Phoenix acquires Paul and Nader. Oklahoma City receives four players and a protected first with a four-year schedule.

transactions.title: Houston changes point guards again.
transactions.text: Westbrook goes to Washington for Wall and a protected future first. Paul’s Houston chapter now has another independent branch.

transactions.title: Four teams. Two stories intersect.
transactions.shortTitle: Harden, Oladipo and LeVert change teams
transactions.text: Harden goes to Brooklyn. Oladipo, part of Indiana’s Paul George return, enters the same exchange. LeVert goes to Indiana.
notes: January 16 is the completed four-team deal. The January 14 three-team announcement was amended after physicals; this is one final package, not two trades of Harden.
The Cleveland/Utah second was initially slated for Brooklyn, but went to Indiana in the final structure. Net movements are recorded, including Vezenkov’s draft rights and Brooklyn cash.
The 2021 and 2025 swap rights interact with prior Oklahoma City rights. No exercise or complete comparison tree for those swaps is claimed here.

transactions.title: Oladipo moves again.
transactions.text: Miami acquires Oladipo. Houston receives Olynyk, Bradley and a conditional swap involving a pick it may hold from Brooklyn.

transactions.title: No. 7: Jonathan Kuminga
transactions.text: Minnesota’s No. 7 is outside the protected top three. Golden State selects Kuminga with the conveyed first.

transactions.title: Beverley leaves with two teammates.
transactions.text: The Clippers send Beverley, Rondo and Oturu to Memphis for Bledsoe.

transactions.title: Nine days. Another trade.
transactions.text: Memphis moves Beverley to Minnesota for Culver and Hernangómez.

transactions.title: Markkanen’s next stop is Cleveland.
transactions.text: A three-team sign-and-trade brings Markkanen to the Cavaliers. Portland receives Nance; Chicago receives Jones and two conditional draft assets.

transactions.title: The extra Dallas first moves again.
transactions.text: Reddish joins Hill, cash and a Brooklyn second on the way to New York. Atlanta receives Knox and a protected Charlotte first.

transactions.title: LeVert becomes three draft paths.
transactions.text: Cleveland adds LeVert and a Miami second. Indiana receives Rubio, a protected first and two seconds.
notes: February 7 is the official acquisition announcement. The teams agreed to the exchange on February 6.

transactions.title: Hart leaves the Davis branch.
transactions.text: Portland sends McCollum, Nance and Snell to New Orleans. Hart joins three players and draft consideration heading west.

transactions.title: Indiana’s other branch goes west.
transactions.text: Sabonis joins Lamb, Justin Holiday and a second-round entitlement. Indiana acquires Haliburton, Hield and Thompson.

transactions.title: Thirteen months later, another exchange.
transactions.text: Harden and Millsap head to Philadelphia. Brooklyn receives Simmons, Curry, Drummond and two first-round obligations.
notes: The 2022/23 choice is a deferral option on one obligation, not two draft picks. The protected later first has a separate fallback.

transactions.title: The extra pick becomes part of another bet.
transactions.shortTitle: Langford joins the Derrick White package
transactions.text: Langford joins Richardson, a first and a swap right. Boston acquires Derrick White; the complete package matters.

transactions.title: Another first survives the lottery.
transactions.text: Cleveland lands at No. 14. Indiana’s first-round entitlement remains protected and rolls to 2023.

resolutions.detail: No. 14 is inside the protected range. The same obligation rolls to Cleveland’s lottery-protected 2023 first.

transactions.title: Brooklyn chooses next year.
transactions.text: The Nets notify the league that they will pass on Philadelphia’s No. 23 and take its 2023 first instead.

resolutions.detail: Brooklyn exercises its option to defer the Philadelphia first from 2022 to 2023. This leaves the 2022 selection with Philadelphia.

transactions.title: No. 17: Tari Eason
transactions.text: The first outright Brooklyn obligation from the Harden package becomes Houston’s No. 17 selection.

transactions.title: No. 12: Jalen Williams
transactions.text: The Clippers’ 2022 first becomes No. 12. Oklahoma City selects Jalen Williams.

transactions.title: No. 31: Andrew Nembhard
transactions.text: Houston’s second, sent to Indiana in the LeVert deal, becomes No. 31 and Andrew Nembhard.

transactions.title: No. 25: Blake Wesley
transactions.text: Boston’s first conveys at No. 25. San Antonio selects Blake Wesley.

transactions.title: Atlanta’s Charlotte right heads to San Antonio.
transactions.text: Murray and Landale go to Atlanta. San Antonio receives Gallinari, the Charlotte obligation and Atlanta’s own future firsts and swap.

transactions.title: Utah puts the return on several timelines.
transactions.shortTitle: Gobert for players, four firsts and a swap
transactions.text: Gobert goes to Minnesota. Utah receives four veterans, Kessler’s draft rights, four first-round obligations and a swap.
notes: The reported July 1 agreement became official July 6. Kessler was an unsigned draft selection, so his rights move separately from signed players.
This route follows the original terms and selected 2022–23 outcomes. Later amendments to Utah’s draft portfolio are not presented as unchanged current ownership.

transactions.title: Before the Holiday package.
transactions.text: Boston acquires Brogdon for five players and a protected first. He will later be part of the separate exchange with Portland.

transactions.title: Beverley reaches the other Los Angeles team.
transactions.text: Utah receives Horton-Tucker and Stanley Johnson for Beverley.

transactions.title: A Brooklyn pick reaches Utah.
transactions.shortTitle: Sexton joins the Donovan Mitchell package
transactions.text: Sexton joins Markkanen, Agbaji and five future draft rights in Cleveland’s package for Donovan Mitchell.
notes: Sexton was signed and traded. September 3 is Cleveland’s official completion date; Utah published its retrospective announcement September 8.
Three outright firsts are unprotected. Later swap amendments and future conveyances are not followed.

transactions.title: Dallas adds another headliner.
transactions.text: Irving and Morris arrive together. Brooklyn receives two players and three future picks. Morris later joins the Luka package.

transactions.title: The headline has four teams behind it.
transactions.shortTitle: Durant goes to Phoenix in a four-team deal
transactions.text: Durant and Warren go to Phoenix. Brooklyn receives Bridges, Johnson and draft capital; Milwaukee gets Crowder; Indiana takes three players, three seconds and cash.
notes: The initial Brooklyn–Phoenix proposal and the Crowder arrangement were combined before completion. Crowder moves directly from Phoenix to Milwaukee in the final package.
All four Phoenix firsts are unprotected. Five Milwaukee-controlled seconds are distributed: two to Brooklyn and three to Indiana.
Trade exceptions are accounting consequences of the transaction, not additional transferable assets received from another franchise.

transactions.title: The Luka and Davis branches meet.
transactions.text: Reddish reaches Portland in a four-team exchange that sends Hart to New York. Their paths began in different headline trades.
notes: Draft rights to Tomić, Diez and Dubljević are part of the exchange. All net destinations in the completed four-team package are retained.
Portland, Philadelphia and Charlotte created traded-player exceptions. Those are generated cap capacity, not assets that can be passed between franchises.
The 2027 composite entitlement is not equated with the isolated New Orleans second from the earlier McCollum trade; a comparison right and an individual pick are different assets.

transactions.title: Poeltl comes back.
transactions.text: Toronto reacquires the center it once sent away. San Antonio receives Birch and three pick obligations.

transactions.title: Three teams find three different exits.
transactions.shortTitle: Russell, Westbrook and the Gobert return meet
transactions.text: The Lakers receive Russell, Beasley and Vanderbilt. Utah takes Westbrook’s package and a protected first. Minnesota receives Conley, Alexander-Walker and three seconds.
notes: Beverley’s separate 2023 deadline trade is outside this route. He is not a member of this eight-player package.
Utah’s later handling of Westbrook’s contract is not represented as another trade.

transactions.title: No. 16: Keyonte George
transactions.text: The first outright selection from the Gobert package becomes No. 16. Utah selects Keyonte George.

transactions.title: No. 23: Kris Murray
transactions.text: New York’s first clears lottery protection. Portland selects Kris Murray at No. 23.

transactions.title: No. 26: Ben Sheppard
transactions.text: One draft later, Cleveland’s obligation conveys at No. 26. Indiana selects Ben Sheppard.

transactions.title: Paul’s next stop is part of a draft-night detour.
transactions.shortTitle: Beal’s three-team deal sends Paul to Washington
transactions.text: Phoenix acquires Beal, Goodwin and Todd. Washington receives Paul, Shamet, Coulibaly’s rights and future draft rights; Indiana moves down one spot and receives two seconds.
notes: June 24 is the final three-team completion. June 18 and June 22 reports described earlier arrangements.
Of Phoenix’s six outgoing seconds, five go to Washington and the 2028 second goes directly to Indiana.
Coulibaly and Walker move as draft rights. The separate Paul–Golden State trade is completed in July.

transactions.title: The point guard reaches Golden State.
transactions.shortTitle: Paul for Poole, players and picks
transactions.text: Washington sends Paul for Poole, Baldwin, Rollins, a protected first, a second and cash. The Poole and draft-asset branches continue toward Dallas and Atlanta.
notes: The 2030 Golden State obligation is the same asset Washington later sends to Dallas in the Davis exchange.
July 6 is the official announcement date in the United States; the NBA summary was updated July 7.

transactions.title: Dame time changes time zones.
transactions.text: Milwaukee gets Lillard. Portland receives Holiday, Ayton, Camara and future rights; Phoenix takes four players.

transactions.title: Four days in Portland.
transactions.text: Holiday is traded again before playing for Portland. Boston sends two players and two first-round obligations.

transactions.title: A third team supplies the second first.
transactions.text: Harden heads to Los Angeles with Tucker and Petrušev. Oklahoma City helps complete Philadelphia’s return by supplying a 2026 first-round entitlement.
notes: November 1 is the completed three-team exchange, following October 31 reports. Players, two outright first-round entitlements, separate swaps, seconds and cash remain one package.

transactions.title: Another New York connection.
transactions.text: Anunoby joins the Knicks with Achiuwa and Flynn. Toronto receives Barrett, Quickley and Detroit’s next second.

transactions.title: A short stop in Indiana.
transactions.text: Indiana acquires Lewis and a second-round entitlement before completing the Siakam trade. His contract can then join Indiana’s outgoing package.
notes: Completed separately before the Toronto exchange. The second stays with Indiana; it is not sent to Toronto.

transactions.title: Indiana adds Siakam.
transactions.text: Three players and three first-round entitlements go to Toronto. Two of those entitlements soon leave distinct traces: a draft selection and another trade package.
notes: Lewis had just been acquired from New Orleans in a separate transaction. The 2024 composite first is one entitlement drawn from a protected comparison pool.

transactions.title: Toronto spends one of the firsts.
transactions.text: The composite pick from the Siakam return joins Lewis and Porter in a new package. Toronto acquires Olynyk and Agbaji together.

transactions.title: No. 29: Isaiah Collier
transactions.text: Oklahoma City’s No. 29 satisfies the composite entitlement. Utah selects Isaiah Collier after acquiring the right from Toronto.

transactions.title: No. 8: Rob Dillingham
transactions.text: Toronto’s first conveys at No. 8. San Antonio selects Dillingham before sending his rights to Minnesota.

transactions.title: No. 3: Reed Sheppard
transactions.text: Brooklyn’s next outright first becomes No. 3. Houston selects Reed Sheppard.

transactions.title: No. 12: Nikola Topić
transactions.text: Five years after the Westbrook exchange, Houston’s first conveys at No. 12. Oklahoma City selects Topić.

transactions.title: No. 19: Ja’Kobe Walter
transactions.text: Indiana’s own first conveys at No. 19. Toronto selects Ja’Kobe Walter.

transactions.title: The eighth pick becomes more time.
transactions.text: Minnesota acquires Dillingham’s rights. San Antonio receives a distant first-round pick and a protected swap right.

transactions.title: No. 31: Jonathan Mogbo
transactions.text: Detroit’s second is the first selection of round two. Toronto uses No. 31 on Jonathan Mogbo.

transactions.title: A new center of gravity.
transactions.text: Towns heads to New York. Minnesota gets three players and a protected first; Charlotte supplies draft rights and takes players, picks and cash.
notes: Charlie Brown Jr., DaQuan Jeffries and Duane Washington Jr. were signed and traded. The Charlotte leg is part of this transaction.

transactions.title: The night nobody saw coming.
transactions.text: Luka changes teams again. Dallas receives Davis, Christie and a future first; Utah is the third team in the exchange.
notes: Cash from Utah facilitates the exchange; amounts are not asserted here. No later use of the 2025 seconds is traced in this story.

transactions.title: Three teams redraw their backcourts.
transactions.text: Fox and McLaughlin go to San Antonio. Sacramento receives LaVine, Cissoko and draft assets; Chicago receives three players and its own first-round obligation back.

resolutions.detail: San Antonio’s conditional claim is cancelled when Chicago reacquires its own first-round obligation.

notes: Finalized February 3, following February 2 reports. Charlotte’s first remains lottery protected in 2025 with the already-documented second-round fallback. Minnesota’s 2031 first is the same right from the Dillingham draft-night trade. Returned own picks are not additional draft slots.

transactions.title: Sacramento repackages part of the return.
transactions.text: Cissoko and the Denver second from the Fox exchange join Sacramento’s 2029 second. Washington sends Valančiūnas in return.
notes: The Kings media guide dates completion February 5. The Denver pick conveys only at positions 34–60.

transactions.title: One headline. Five teams.
transactions.text: Butler goes to Golden State. Follow the entire exchange to see why Miami, Utah, Detroit and Toronto all appear in the same frame.
notes: This scene records net transfers in the completed five-team package; Schröder was routed through Utah. Martin had arrived in Detroit in a separate Philadelphia deal, outside this story.
Some minor second-round terms were not disclosed. Their announced consideration is retained, clearly labelled, with no invented origins or outcomes.

transactions.title: Two branches become another package.
transactions.text: Brown and the Indiana first came from the Siakam deal. Olynyk arrived through the next exchange. Toronto combines them with a second-round pick for Ingram.

transactions.title: The Harden first changes hands.
transactions.text: Philadelphia sends the same 2026 entitlement with Jackson to Washington. Its return is Jared Butler and four second-round entitlements.
notes: This records the final completed package, including Jared Butler and all four seconds. Earlier cash-only summaries are incomplete.

transactions.title: No. 17: Joan Beringer
transactions.text: Detroit’s first clears its top-13 protection. Minnesota uses No. 17 on Joan Beringer.

transactions.title: No. 20: Kasparas Jakučionis
transactions.text: The Golden State first conveys at No. 20. Miami selects Kasparas Jakučionis.

transactions.title: No. 40: Micah Peavy
transactions.text: The Phoenix second from the Beal exchange becomes No. 40. Washington selects Peavy, whose rights join the subsequent Poole–McCollum package.

transactions.title: No. 42: Maxime Raynaud
transactions.text: The Chicago second acquired in the Fox exchange conveys at No. 42. Sacramento selects Maxime Raynaud.

transactions.title: Sexton’s branch reaches Charlotte.
transactions.text: One player from Cleveland’s Mitchell package moves again. Utah pairs Sexton with a second-round entitlement to acquire Nurkić.
notes: Charlotte’s dated announcement and the completed-trade report establish June 29 in the United States. Some league summaries label the transaction June 30. Nurkić’s earlier acquisition by Charlotte and Sexton’s later career are outside this route.

transactions.title: Washington enters the thread.
transactions.text: McCollum moves to Washington in a three-team package. Chicago’s 2027 second also arrives—and later joins the Davis return to Dallas.
notes: The final July 6 package includes Houston and Mojave King’s draft rights; the initial two-team report is incomplete.

transactions.title: A second arrival in Portland.
transactions.text: Portland reacquires Holiday for Simons. The completed deal is a player-for-player exchange; the draft picks in earlier reports were removed.

transactions.title: Brooklyn turns another piece into a distant first.
transactions.shortTitle: Cameron Johnson for Porter + a 2032 first
transactions.text: Johnson, acquired in the Durant package, goes to Denver. Brooklyn receives Porter and an unprotected 2032 first.
notes: July 8 is the completed announcement date confirmed by Brooklyn and contemporaneous reporting. Denver’s page contains a conflicting July 6 dateline; its publication timestamp is July 8.
Durant’s own subsequent Houston move is outside this bounded route. The 2025 endpoint follows Johnson, not an assertion that Durant remained in Phoenix.

transactions.title: Olynyk takes one more turn.
transactions.text: Washington sends Olynyk to San Antonio for Branham, Wesley and a composite second-round entitlement. Both guards belong to the same outgoing package.

transactions.title: Denver and Sacramento exchange centers.
transactions.text: Valančiūnas moves to Denver for Šarić. The final exchange includes no additional draft consideration.
notes: July 13 is the official completed-trade date. July 1 was the reported agreement. Šarić’s intervening career after Minnesota is outside this route.

transactions.title: Atlanta’s path turns toward D.C.
transactions.text: The other player from draft night leaves Atlanta. Washington sends back two players; no draft pick is included.

transactions.title: Harden’s route reaches Cleveland.
transactions.text: The Cavaliers exchange Garland and their 2026 second for Harden. This is a separate branch from the first-round entitlement still moving through other deals.

transactions.title: Different paths. Same destination.
transactions.text: Davis follows Trae to Washington through a separate trade. The two branches meet in a city neither started in.
notes: The final three-team structure is recorded. The 2026 entitlement compares Oklahoma City, Houston and the Clippers. Coverage ends February 5, before the draft.

stories.title: The Luka ripple
stories.headline:
TWO PICKS.
TWO FUTURES.
stories.subtitle: A draft-night exchange. Two careers. An afterlife nobody could have drawn up.
stories.coverage: Traces Luka, Trae and the Dallas first through Reddish; the Reddish–Hart exchange joins the 2019 Davis branch. Follows New York’s first to Kris Murray and McCollum into Washington’s 2026 Trae exchange. Stops February 5, 2026. Other pick rights and secondary player branches are untraced.
stories.takeaway: The draft-night package opens several paths. Follow one asset at a time.
stories.imageAlt: Luka Dončić playing for Dallas in 2021

stories.title: The night Dallas changed
stories.headline:
ONE NIGHT.
TWO CORNERSTONES.
stories.subtitle: Dirk’s draft rights. Garrity’s next stop. The separate deal that brought Nash.
stories.coverage: Follows the separate Dirk and Nash draft-night packages, Dallas’s 1999 first to Marion, and Marion through Miami and Toronto back to Dallas in July 2009. Shaq’s Miami, Phoenix and Cleveland exchanges are shared intersections. Conditional Toronto picks and other branches stop at their recorded transfers; Nash’s free agency is not a trade return.
stories.takeaway: Pat Garrity’s rights connect the two deals. Each package still matters.
stories.imageAlt: Dirk Nowitzki playing for Dallas in 2009

stories.title: Brooklyn buys the present
stories.headline:
THE LONG
GAME.
stories.subtitle: Three firsts, one swap, and the patience between a promise and a player.
stories.coverage: Follows the Brooklyn picks to Young, Brown, the Tatum trade-down, Sexton’s Donovan Mitchell package, and Langford’s Derrick White package through September 3, 2022. White’s 2022 first becomes Blake Wesley. Other player moves, later swap amendments and future picks are untraced.
stories.takeaway: A swap is a right to exchange picks. Boston still needed another trade to reach No. 3.
stories.imageAlt: Kevin Garnett playing for Boston in 2008

stories.title: Thirteen to Los Angeles
stories.headline:
BEFORE
THE LEGEND.
stories.subtitle: A draft selection in Charlotte. A rights transfer two weeks later.
stories.coverage: The June 26 selection and July 11, 1996 Bryant–Divac exchange only. This is a short origin story; later free agency is outside the trade graph.
stories.takeaway: Draft night and the effective trade date are not always the same day.

stories.title: The dynasty splits
stories.headline:
THE BIG
AFTERLIFE.
stories.subtitle: From Shaq’s move to Miami to two very different Gasol destinations.
stories.coverage: Follows both Shaq pick returns, Marion’s Dallas route, Butler’s Dallas exchange, the Gasol packages, and the Lakers 2010 first through Vásquez to Powell rights, Anunoby and Mogbo. Stops June 27, 2024. Untraced obligations are labelled; no free agency or shared championship is treated as a trade connection.
stories.takeaway: The connection runs through whole packages, with additional assets entering each time.

stories.title: The brothers in the fine print
stories.headline:
A TALE OF
TWO GASOLS.
stories.subtitle: One brother headlines the trade. The other appears as draft rights.
stories.coverage: Follows Marc to Toronto and the Lakers 2010 first to Vásquez, then his New Orleans, Sacramento, Toronto and Milwaukee exchanges. The Clippers first becomes Anunoby; the later Knicks package’s Detroit second becomes Mogbo. Stops June 27, 2024. The Lakers 2008 first and other side branches remain untraced.
stories.takeaway: A draft-rights entry in one deal can become the headliner of another.

stories.title: Boston’s two big swings
stories.headline:
ALL IN.
THEN RESET.
stories.subtitle: The 2007 arrival and the 2013 departure belong to different Boston bets.
stories.coverage: Follows the Brooklyn picks to Young, Brown, the Tatum trade-down, Sexton’s Donovan Mitchell package, and Langford’s Derrick White package through September 3, 2022. White’s 2022 first becomes Blake Wesley. Other player moves, later swap amendments and future picks are untraced.
stories.takeaway: Returning a team’s own pick obligation extinguishes a claim; it creates no extra pick.
stories.imageAlt: Kevin Garnett playing for Boston in 2008

stories.title: Houston finds its headliner
stories.headline:
THE BET
ON THIRTEEN.
stories.subtitle: The player went to Houston. Three very different draft promises went the other way.
stories.coverage: From Houston’s 2012 acquisition through the completed 2021 four-team exchange and 2022 Philadelphia deal. Selected pick branches become Adams, Abrines, McGary, Eason, Nembhard, Ben Sheppard and Reed Sheppard. Stops June 26, 2024; later player moves, swap amendments and unused fallback terms are untraced.
stories.takeaway: A protected pick can survive one draft and convey at the next. It is still one obligation.

stories.title: The return trip
stories.headline:
A LEAP.
A LOOP.
stories.subtitle: Kawhi goes north. Years later, Poeltl’s branch circles back to Toronto.
stories.coverage: Follows Keldon Johnson and Poeltl’s return, then Toronto’s No. 8 into the Dillingham rights trade. Stops June 26, 2024 with Minnesota’s future first and swap outstanding at that point.
stories.takeaway: A returning player can open a new branch years after the original exchange.

stories.title: The price of right now
stories.headline:
FIVE FIRSTS.
ONE FUTURE.
stories.subtitle: George arrives in Oklahoma City, then leaves in a very different kind of deal.
stories.coverage: Both sides of Indiana’s George return are followed: Sabonis into the Haliburton package; Oladipo through the four-team Harden deal, LeVert, Nembhard and Ben Sheppard. Includes the full Clippers package and Jalen Williams. Stops June 22, 2023; other picks and intervening free agency are untraced.
stories.takeaway: Shai and the draft obligations arrive in the same package. Their later paths remain distinct.

stories.title: The Davis chain
stories.headline:
THREE CITIES.
THREE DEALS.
stories.subtitle: New Orleans to Los Angeles. Dallas to Washington. Follow the actual packages.
stories.coverage: The Davis route from 2019 through February 2026, plus Hart into the Reddish exchange and New York’s first into Kris Murray. McCollum’s New Orleans–Washington–Atlanta path is included, as is Chicago’s second through Washington to Dallas. Other rights are untraced beyond their displayed transactions.
stories.takeaway: Washington appears in the first deal as a facilitator and in the last as Davis’s destination.

stories.title: Another Dallas crossroads
stories.headline:
TWO STARS.
MORE THREADS.
stories.subtitle: Kyrie’s arrival includes Markieff Morris. Follow the less obvious thread.
stories.coverage: Follows Morris from the Kyrie package into the Luka deal, then Davis into Washington. This is not a claim that Kyrie was traded for any of those returns. Brooklyn’s picks are untraced.
stories.takeaway: Shared teammates can connect trades whose headline players never change hands for one another.

stories.title: Four days in Portland
stories.headline:
THE HOLIDAY
DETOUR.
stories.subtitle: Dame moves to Milwaukee. Jrue’s Portland stop turns out to be very short.
stories.coverage: Includes Brogdon’s 2022 Boston arrival as backward context for the 2023 Holiday package, then Lillard’s three-team trade, Holiday to Boston and the July 7, 2025 Simons exchange. Future draft rights and other player branches are untraced.
stories.takeaway: The final 2025 exchange contains no draft picks; early reports described a different proposal.

stories.title: A new center of gravity
stories.headline:
BIG MAN.
BIGGER PACKAGE.
stories.subtitle: The New York–Minnesota headline has a Charlotte chapter, too.
stories.coverage: The complete October 2, 2024 three-team trade and Detroit’s first conveying to Minnesota as No. 17 in 2025. Other players and second-round outcomes are untraced.
stories.takeaway: The original franchise of a traded pick can be a team that did not participate in this deal.

stories.title: Five teams, one headline
stories.headline:
THE FIVE-TEAM
SHUFFLE.
stories.subtitle: A deadline blockbuster whose edges reach far beyond Miami and Golden State.
stories.coverage: The final February 6 five-team package and the Golden State first becoming Miami’s No. 20. Some minor second-round terms were undisclosed; those assets are labelled and left untraced.
stories.takeaway: A headline is an entry point. The full exchange is the story.

stories.title: The Kidd round trip
stories.headline: A long way home.
stories.subtitle: Dallas to Phoenix. New Jersey to Dallas. Follow the packages, then watch one Dallas pick travel with Vince Carter.
stories.coverage: Kidd’s three trades, the Cassell branch, two verified Dallas/Phoenix pick conveyances and Ryan Anderson’s Orlando exchange. Stops with Carter’s 2010 Phoenix package; later free agency and other pick branches are untraced.
stories.takeaway: The Dallas first in Kidd’s return package became Ryan Anderson, who later traveled to Orlando with Vince Carter.

stories.title: Vince changes the picture
stories.headline: The next flight.
stories.subtitle: Toronto, New Jersey, Orlando, Phoenix. Follow Vince—and the first-round pick whose route begins in Dallas.
stories.coverage: Three Carter trades, Joey Graham’s Philadelphia-origin pick and the Dallas origin of Ryan Anderson’s selection. Stops in December 2010; remaining picks and subsequent free-agent signings are untraced.
stories.takeaway: Carter and Anderson were a two-player package. Anderson’s draft pick had come from Dallas in a different star’s trade.

stories.title: The clause that kept going
stories.headline: Five years in the fine print.
stories.subtitle: A star to New York. A swap that becomes Jamal Murray. And the other pick’s route into Toronto’s Kawhi package.
stories.coverage: The final 2011 package, selected 2012/2016/2018 pick outcomes, Anthony’s 2017/2018 trades, and Poeltl’s existing route through the 2024 draft. Other players, seconds, the 2014 first and the protected OKC 2022 obligation are not followed after their displayed transfers.
stories.takeaway: Denver’s swap and Toronto’s separate Bargnani trade divided two firsts. Murray and Poeltl are documented outcomes of different entitlements.

stories.title: Barkley’s Dallas connection
stories.headline: Follow Sam Cassell.
stories.subtitle: Barkley goes to Houston. One player in Phoenix’s return soon becomes part of Dallas’s Jason Kidd exchange.
stories.coverage: Both Barkley trades, Cassell’s Phoenix–Dallas–New Jersey route, the Kidd exchange and the Phoenix second’s 1998 conveyance. Stops at Kidd’s 2001 New Jersey arrival; Horry and other received assets remain bounded branches.
stories.takeaway: Cassell connects the Barkley and Kidd packages. That does not mean Barkley alone was exchanged for everything that followed.

stories.title: The original giant moves
stories.headline: Even Wilt was traded.
stories.subtitle: Two blockbuster exchanges, three franchises. Follow Chamberlain from San Francisco to Philadelphia to Los Angeles.
stories.coverage: Only the complete 1965 and 1968 Chamberlain packages. Cash is included without invented amounts. Earlier franchise relocation and subsequent player transactions are outside the selected route.
stories.takeaway: The San Francisco Warriors and Philadelphia 76ers were separate franchises. These were two trades, not a franchise returning home.

stories.title: The Chris Paul trail
stories.headline:
One point guard.
A league of echoes.
stories.subtitle: From Lob City to a draft obligation that reaches Dallas. Follow Paul, then follow what travels the other way.
stories.coverage: Paul’s completed 2011, 2017, 2019, 2020 and two 2023 trades; selected Rivers, Topić, Peavy, Poole and draft-asset branches through February 2026. Paul’s later free agency and untraced draft outcomes are excluded.
stories.takeaway: A single career can connect very different packages. The players and picks received alongside each other remain separate paths.

stories.title: The other side of Lob City
stories.headline:
Follow the return.
Find another blockbuster.
stories.subtitle: Beverley reaches the Gobert package. Houston’s first reaches Golden State. Both begin in the same Clippers return.
stories.coverage: Two traced branches of the 2017 Paul package: the Houston first through Spellman and the Russell–Wiggins exchange; Beverley through Minnesota and the Gobert package. Stops at the 2023 draft. Other players and subsequent moves are outside the route.
stories.takeaway: The least famous pieces can reveal the longest connections. A later package still includes contributions from several assets.

stories.title: The Westbrook exchange
stories.headline:
Two point guards.
Years of consequences.
stories.subtitle: Houston and Oklahoma City exchange stars. The picks, and Paul’s next trades, keep the story moving.
stories.coverage: The 2019 exchange, Westbrook’s 2020 Washington move, Topić’s 2024 selection and Paul-return branches through February 2026. Westbrook’s Lakers arrival and subsequent career are outside this route. Original future-pick terms are recorded; untraced outcomes are not current holdings.
stories.takeaway: An exchange of stars can leave several independent trails. The Houston first and the Paul package have different afterlives.

stories.title: What Durant left behind
stories.headline:
A goodbye.
Several new beginnings.
stories.subtitle: Russell’s package brings Wiggins and a pick. Johnson’s next move brings a first seven years away.
stories.coverage: Durant’s 2019 sign-and-trade and 2023 Phoenix package; selected Russell, Wiggins, Kuminga and Cameron Johnson branches through July 2025. Durant’s 2025 Houston deal, the Bridges branch and remaining pick outcomes are not traced. Later player movement is not implied absent.
stories.takeaway: The 2020 return belongs to the Russell–Spellman–Evans package. Durant’s departure connects to that package without becoming its sole cause.

stories.title: The Gobert package
stories.headline:
One center.
Several futures.
stories.subtitle: Utah receives players, draft rights and obligations. Follow the routes that separate almost immediately.
stories.coverage: Beverley’s 2021 route into Minnesota, the complete July 2022 Gobert transaction, Beverley’s Lakers move, the February 2023 three-team package and the Keyonte George selection. Later Utah pick pooling, trades and conveyances are outside this story.
stories.takeaway: Four future firsts, one swap and an already-drafted player are different assets. Beasley and Vanderbilt later join a package with other contributions.

stories.title: Kareem changes coast
stories.headline:
The skyhook.
The other side.
stories.subtitle: A Los Angeles landmark begins with six names. Follow one of Milwaukee’s rookies into a second six-player trade.
stories.coverage: The complete 1975 exchange and Bridgeman’s inclusion in the 1984 Clippers–Bucks package. Stops September 29, 1984; later trades and career milestones are not treated as trade returns.
stories.takeaway: Bridgeman’s rights were one part of Milwaukee’s return. Nine years later, he joined a package for Cummings, Hodges and Pierce.

stories.title: Pippen’s Dallas detour
stories.headline:
Follow the six
who came back.
stories.subtitle: Seattle to Chicago to Houston to Portland. Then follow Kelvin Cato, a Dallas draft choice in Pippen’s six-player return.
stories.coverage: Pippen’s three trades, Cato’s Dallas origin, the complete McGrady packages, and the Jordan Hill–Dallas first–Harden route through 2014. The early Pippen draft considerations have untraced terms; no unsupported selection is assigned.
stories.takeaway: Cato connects Pippen’s Portland trade to McGrady’s Houston arrival. Hill and a protected Dallas first carry a later branch into the Harden package.

stories.title: The Worm changes sides
stories.headline:
Detroit.
San Antonio. Chicago.
stories.subtitle: Two Rodman trades, Elliott’s return, and the small considerations that a headline leaves out.
stories.coverage: Rodman’s 1993 and 1995 exchanges, the separate same-day Morris deal, and Elliott’s completed July 1994 return. Stops October 2, 1995. Conditional seconds and swap outcomes are untraced; the additional 1995 consideration is explicitly undisclosed.
stories.takeaway: Elliott returned to San Antonio before Rodman left. These are separate completed exchanges, not a reversal that erased the first package.

stories.title: The Answer’s next questions
stories.headline:
A pick connects
two superstar trades.
stories.subtitle: Iverson leaves Philadelphia. A Denver first becomes Cook, who travels through Miami into the Harden exchange.
stories.coverage: Both Iverson trades, Denver’s 2007 first to Cook, Cook’s Miami and Oklahoma City packages, and shared Carmelo/Harden exchanges. Stops October 27, 2012; Dallas’s 2007 first and later pick branches are untraced.
stories.takeaway: Cook and Billups connect different sides of Iverson’s history to Harden and Carmelo. Each arrives in a package with other contributions.

stories.title: T-Mac’s branching return
stories.headline:
The names behind
the headline.
stories.subtitle: McGrady’s trades branch toward Ariza, Martin and a protected Dallas first. Follow the entire packages to see where the paths meet.
stories.coverage: The complete 2004 and 2010 McGrady trades; Francis to Ariza; Hill to the Dallas first; Odom’s 2012 second and its rights return; the shared Harden package and 2014 McGary conveyance. New York’s first conveys to Royce White. The 2011 New York swap and the Odom 2013 second-round swap remain bounded, untraced branches.
stories.takeaway: The Dallas first traveled through the Odom and Hill trades before joining Houston’s offer for Harden. It remained one obligation throughout.

stories.title: Harden, again.
stories.headline: One star. Another city. A first still moving.
stories.subtitle: Follow Harden to Los Angeles and Cleveland, then follow a different part of the return all the way to Dallas.
stories.coverage: The 2022 Philadelphia arrival, final 2023 three-team Clippers exchange, the 2025 transfer of its composite first and two separate February 2026 endpoints. Later selection, swap exercise and other outgoing-player careers are untraced.
stories.takeaway: The 2026 first that Philadelphia received for Harden later joins Washington’s Anthony Davis package. Harden himself takes a different route.

stories.title: The Mitchell exchange.
stories.headline: One arrival. Three paths out.
stories.subtitle: Cleveland’s big swing connects a draft-night gamble, Chicago’s rebuild and the next moves in Utah.
stories.coverage: Mitchell’s 2017 draft-rights arrival, Markkanen’s Chicago and Cleveland moves, the complete 2022 Cleveland–Utah exchange, Agbaji’s Toronto package and Sexton’s 2025 Charlotte trade. Utah’s later first-round pools and actual swap exercise are untraced.
stories.takeaway: Cleveland acquires one star in a package. Utah’s player branches later reach Toronto and Charlotte, each through a separate complete exchange.

stories.title: Fox. LaVine. The next move.
stories.headline: Three backcourts change in one night.
stories.subtitle: Follow the February 2025 exchange backward through its picks and forward to Sacramento’s next center.
stories.coverage: The final Fox–LaVine three-team exchange, selected prior LaVine and pick transfers, the complete Valančiūnas packages, and Chicago’s second-round conveyance as Raynaud. Charlotte’s eventual fallback and other first-round fulfillment remain untraced.
stories.takeaway: Two rights acquired in earlier San Antonio deals join the Fox exchange. Sacramento then combines two incoming pieces with another pick for Valančiūnas.

stories.title: Siakam’s second act.
stories.headline: Toronto’s return keeps moving.
stories.subtitle: A first becomes Walter. Another helps acquire Olynyk and Agbaji. A later package brings Ingram north.
stories.coverage: The two separate January 2024 trades, both 2024 first-round conveyances, Ingram’s complete 2025 package, and selected Olynyk/McCollum/Branham moves through February 2026. The Indiana first’s later transfers and fulfillment are untraced.
stories.takeaway: Toronto reuses different pieces of the Siakam return in different packages. Those packages connect Toronto, Utah, New Orleans, Washington and San Antonio.

stories.title: Before Miami, a fork.
stories.headline: Butler goes one way. LaVine and Markkanen another.
stories.subtitle: The 2017 Chicago rebuild has branches that meet the 2022 Mitchell and 2025 Fox trades.
stories.coverage: Butler’s complete 2017, 2018 and 2019 trades, plus the LaVine and Markkanen branches into Fox and Mitchell packages. Butler’s own path stops at Miami in 2019; his separate 2025 Warriors story is available in the wider web. Remaining outgoing-player careers and pick resolutions are untraced.
stories.takeaway: The player Chicago sends away and the players it receives continue through independent packages. Neither branch alone explains the other’s outcomes.
